c.tagline: Ancient empires and chaos in India's capital.

taxi.fareNote: Meters often ignored; app cabs dominant

emergency.note: 100 (police) and 108 (ambulance) also work; English-speaking operators are common in Delhi.

hood_landmark.Connaught Place: colonial-era white colonnades circling Central Park
hood_landmark.Chandni Chowk: the Red Fort rising at the bazaar's eastern end
hood_landmark.Hauz Khas: Hauz Khas Fort and its medieval reservoir beside Deer Park
hood_landmark.Karol Bagh: Ajmal Khan Road's bustling shopping bazaar
hood_landmark.Saket: Select Citywalk mall, with the Qutub Minar close by

avoid.reason: Pervasive touts/scams around New Delhi station, Connaught Place and Paharganj (fake tourist offices, "hotel closed" taxi tricks); pickpocketing; women should take extra care at night

hood_desc: Connaught Place is the colonial-era circular commercial heart of New Delhi, packed with shops, restaurants and offices. It suits first-time visitors who want a central base with easy metro access and plenty to see on foot.

Chandni Chowk is the chaotic, sensory-overload heart of Old Delhi near the Red Fort, famous for street food, spice bazaars and narrow historic lanes. It is best for foodies and history lovers who embrace crowds and noise, not those seeking calm or comfort.
Hauz Khas is a trendy urban village in South Delhi wrapped around medieval ruins and a lake, full of boutiques, rooftop bars and cafes. It suits younger travelers, creatives and nightlife seekers.

Karol Bagh is a bustling mid-range district known for its jewelry, clothing and electronics markets plus value hotels. It suits budget to mid-range travelers who want good shopping and solid metro links.

Saket is an upscale, planned South Delhi neighborhood with big malls like Select Citywalk, corporate offices and proximity to Qutub Minar. It suits affluent shoppers, business travelers and families wanting modern amenities and a quieter feel.
lodging: The Rose Boutique Hotel Hauz Khas
Country Inn and Suites by Radisson New Delhi Saket

water.note: Avoid tap water; use sealed bottled or purified water, including for brushing teeth.

transit.pay: Get a rechargeable smart card (increasingly the NCMC/One Delhi card) at any station customer-care counter for about ₹200 (~$2.40, including a refundable deposit), then tap in/out; QR-code tickets are also sold at machines and the DMRC app. Fares range roughly ₹10-60 (~$0.12-0.72) depending on distance.
transit.hours: Trains generally run from about 5-5:30am until 11:30pm-midnight, with services roughly every 3-10 minutes at peak.

transit.m: Airport Express (Orange Line) metro to New Delhi station, then short hop to Connaught Place, approx 20-25 min
Airport Express metro to Shivaji Stadium station (edge of Connaught Place), approx 25-30 min
